rationales: Establishing a theory comes after the issue has been identified.
Implementing a solution happens after the cause and plan have been determined.
Identifying the problem is the first step in the troubleshooting process.
Documenting findings and outcomes is typically the final step.
Saving money on repairs can be a benefit, but it is not the main reason effective troubleshooting matters.
Troubleshooting does not prevent the need for professional help in every situation.
Effective troubleshooting helps systems operate smoothly and efficiently.
Troubleshooting is not primarily intended to enable more frequent system updates.
Testing a theory determines whether it is correct rather than creating the theory.
Establishing a theory of probable cause means proposing what might be causing the problem.
Implementing a solution occurs after the cause and resolution plan are established.
Verifying functionality checks the system after a solution has been implemented.
Documentation follows verification of the system’s functionality.
Testing the theory takes place before implementing a solution.
Verifying full system functionality is the next step after implementing a solution.
Establishing a plan of action happens before implementing the solution.
Testing a battery is an action taken to investigate a problem, not an example of initially identifying it.
Planning to replace a battery is part of deciding how to resolve a problem.
Noticing that the laptop does not turn on describes identifying the problem.
Writing down a battery replacement is documenting an action and its outcome.
Documentation may support later troubleshooting, but its primary purpose is to keep a record rather than directly solve problems faster.
Recording findings, actions, and outcomes provides useful information for future reference.
Documentation does not itself make testing more efficient.
Documentation records what was done but does not ensure the solution was implemented correctly.
The problem is identified in an earlier step, before making a plan of action.
Verifying full functionality occurs after the solution is implemented.
Determining the cause is part of testing the theory, before establishing a plan of action.
A plan of action determines the steps needed to resolve the issue.
Troubleshooting may reveal outdated hardware, but it does not ensure components are always up to date.
Troubleshooting does not eliminate the need for data backups.
Troubleshooting helps keep computing systems running smoothly and securely by identifying and resolving issues.
Troubleshooting does not eliminate the need for software updates.
Troubleshooting can reduce the need for outside help in some cases, but that is not the main issue it prevents.
Troubleshooting does not remove the need for software updates.
Quickly identifying and resolving issues helps prevent downtime and lost productivity.
Troubleshooting does not eliminate the need for regular maintenance.
Finding a bug that produces incorrect database results helps protect the accuracy and integrity of data.
Replacing a faulty printer addresses a hardware issue but does not specifically ensure data integrity.
Using a cooling pad helps prevent overheating rather than protect data accuracy.
Regularly updating an operating system can improve security and performance, but it is not specifically an example of ensuring data integrity through troubleshooting.
